title: The Abyss and the Provision of God
english: To show this regarding the order of the angels, although is it not somewhat different for all of them? Ps 103,1: He clothed himself in majesty, and to those in greatness and those who exalt themselves, he gives the appropriate thing; but in confession, he gives to all a harmonious symphony concerning them. For the name of confession signifies also the symphony that is in words. But if you wish him to be clothed in another kind of confession according to repentance and in thanksgiving, it is not for sinners. Corresponding to this signified thing, he will also clothe the virtue of those who succeed, which is called majesty. And just as the Savior says, 'I am naked, and you clothed me' (Matt 25:36), this shows what his clothing and covering becomes: the practice of those living according to him; so also the Father will clothe himself in the virtues of those who strive concerning him.

Ps 103,2a: Just as one who puts on a sensible garment is covered from every side, so God, being filled with knowledge from every side, as his essence turns out to be ungraspable, puts on light as a garment, signifying even here the most sharp-witted knowledge of the light. Agreeing with this concerning God, Paul writes that he has an unapproachable light, or dwells in unapproachable light (1 Tim 6:16). For in this very expression, it is said that the whole is the knowledge of God, and for this reason, that it is difficult to understand for the intellects, that he dwells in unapproachable light.

Ps 103,2b.3a: He roofs the air above us and the wind toward the ether with waters according to the swirling of the clouds. And toward the intellect: he calls the intellectual essence 'heaven,' being stretched out and made simple upon the canopy of the mind, he who roofs the intellectual and divine things with waters, the heavenly things of the soul, that is, its powers which happen to be above the sensible.

Ps 103,6a: You will find the abyss lying upon ungraspability, and in 'Your judgments, O Lord, are many' (Ps 136:7), for his judgments being unsearchable, there is no grasping of them. Therefore also not simply ab...

They are compared to a small abyss, but a great one. And God is not a small abyss, for the greatness of the abyss covers the judgments of the enclosure, being called incomprehensibility. Ps 103:7b: Hearing the sound of thunder—that is, the word being made loudly according to providence—they shall fear. It is fitting that these things should be said concerning the visible things and the waters. It is possible to take 'From the sound of thunder they shall fear' (Ps 103:11) not concerning the waters, but concerning men, rather concerning all living creatures, as it might happen that a thunder, of the invisible and unseen divinity, is perceived.

Through every word the preceding psalm glorifies and doxologizes God, remembering each of the creatures; and God, accepting his providence in the things set forth, marvels and considers his goodness with wisdom, caring for the endurance of the irrational animals. And rightly; for if he himself has made them, he is the provider of both their food and their drink. Ps 103:13–15.

And by ascent you shall understand the words having been fully returned; for the spirit-bearing men are they. They are watered from the heavenly things of this God, being filled with the gifts of the Spirit, the word of wisdom, and the following things which are innumerable. And the heavenly things of God, from which the words water, are sharp and surpassing contemplations of the truth, being called heavenly because they have not ascended beyond themselves. 'The earth shall be satisfied from the fruit of your works.' For he is... Let the earth blossom with grass for pasture and a fruitful tree producing fruit, and the following. And by ascent from Jesus, having much fruit during the visitation, the whole earth is satisfied, receiving those things having been made by Jesus in such a paradoxical way. For this is the fruit of his works.
